bodyMarkdown:
If you live with ADHD-style distraction, the best app blocker for Android is not the one that looks strictest. It is the one you will actually start, trust and keep using when the urge to switch apps shows up.

For a lot of people, the problem is not a lack of willpower. The problem is speed. The distraction happens before you have time to think, and by the time a warning shows up, the feed is already open.

## What an ADHD-friendly app blocker needs to do

Look for four things:

- Fast setup. If it takes more than a few taps, you will skip it when you are rushed.
- Real-time blocking. The block should happen when the app opens, not after you have already started scrolling.
- Recovery after a slip. One distraction should not turn into a ruined day.
- A clear session boundary. ADHD brains do better when there is a visible start and end.

That is why simple timers and screen time dashboards often fall short. They can tell you what happened later, but they do not help much in the exact moment when your attention slips.

## Why warnings alone do not hold up

Warnings are easy to dismiss. Screen time summaries are useful for patterns, but they do not interrupt the impulse.

If you already know which apps pull you away, you need a blocker that acts during the session. That is the difference between a tool that reports distraction and a tool that helps stop it.

## What CogniFocus does differently

CogniFocus is built around active focus sessions. You start a session, Shield turns on and blocked apps are intercepted during that window. CogniFocus is free to start on Android and it reacts when your attention slips, not just after the fact.

The other piece is what happens after a block. CogniFocus does not treat a single distraction like a total failure. It helps you return to the session instead of throwing the whole block away.

If you want less noise during the session, DND Focus Mode helps silence interruptions while you work.

## A simple setup that works better than overblocking

Start small.

1. Pick the two or three apps that actually derail you.
2. Set a short session, not a huge one.
3. Start the blocker before you begin the task.
4. Keep your goal visible so you know what the session is for.
5. When you slip, get back to work instead of restarting everything.

That setup works better than blocking every app on your phone. Overblocking usually makes people quit the blocker, then quit the session.

## The short version

If you need an app blocker for ADHD on Android, choose one that starts quickly, blocks in real time and helps you recover after a distraction. That is the part most tools miss.

CogniFocus was made for that exact loop. It combines a focus timer, app blocking and a Goblin companion that reacts when you drift.
